mainTopic: Animals that are forbidden for the מזבח (but not forbidden to use for other things) getting mixed up with קרבנות
overview: This text is the middle of a list in the משנה. The משנה names animals that can never be brought on the מזבח, even though a person is generally allowed to get use from them. The concern is a case where one of these animals gets mixed into a group of קרבנות and no one can tell which one it is. First the משנה names an ox that killed a person, where the only proof is one witness or the owner's own admission. With two witnesses, the ox would have been stoned and forbidden for any use. Next it lists three pairs of animals connected to sin: animals involved in bestiality, animals connected to עבודה זרה, and an animal given as a harlot's payment or traded for a dog. The משנה gives its ruling for such a mix right after this list.

steps.title: An ox that killed a person but was not convicted by two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה goes on with its list. If קרבנות got mixed with an ox that killed a person, and the only proof is one witness or the owner's own admission, that ox still causes a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If the קרבנות got mixed with an ox] that killed a person, according to one witness or according to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is still in the middle of its list of animals that might get mixed in with קרבנות. Here it adds an ox that killed someone but was never sentenced to סקילה. The ruling for all these cases comes later in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To sentence an ox to סקילה, two witnesses are needed. If there was only one witness, or only the owner admitted it, the ox is not killed and people may still get use from it. Still, it may not be brought on the מזבח, so mixing it with קרבנות causes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness. Not enough to sentence the ox
Based on the owner's own admission
An ox sentenced to stoning, which is forbidden for any use. This one is different because it was never sentenced

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this ox up with a שור הנסקל, an ox that was actually sentenced. A sentenced ox is forbidden for any use. This ox is only forbidden for the מזבח, and that is why the משנה lists it separately.

phrases.notes: The word for 'with an ox' (בשור) is at the end of the previous עמוד, so this line finishes that sentence.
The owner admitted his ox killed someone; two witnesses never testified.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהֵמִית אֶת הָאָדָם עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד אוֹ עַל פִּי הַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list from the previous עמוד, where it started the case of an ox mixed with קרבנות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that killed a person, with proof only from one witness or from the owner, is one of the animals that is a problem when mixed with קרבנות. It is not sentenced to death, but it is not fit for the מזבח.

steps.title: More animals connected to sin that cannot be brought on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds three pairs to its list: animals involved in bestiality, animals connected to עבודה זרה, and animals given as a harlot's payment or traded for a dog.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an animal that had relations with a person, or that a person had relations with. With an animal set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped. With a harlot's payment, or the price of a dog.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps building its list of animals that might get mixed into a group of קרבנות. It is setting things up for the ruling that comes right after the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these animals is unfit for the מזבח because it was connected to a sin, but it is not forbidden for everyday use. For רובע and נרבע this works like the ox: the act is known only from one witness or the owner, because with two witnesses the animal would be stoned and forbidden for any use. The pairs are bestiality (רובע and נרבע), idol worship (מוקצה and נעבד), and money from forbidden sources (אתנן and מחיר).

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that had relations with a person, or that a person had relations with
An animal set aside to be offered to an idol
An animal that was itself worshipped as a god
An animal given as payment to a harlot
An animal received in trade for a dog

steps.whatToRemember: Every animal on this list may be used for everyday things, but it can never go on the מזבח. When one gets mixed into a group of קרבנות, we cannot tell which animals are fit to offer.

phrases.english: with an animal that copulated with a person, or one that was the object of bestiality,
with one set aside for idol worship, or one that was worshipped,
with a harlot's payment, or the price of a dog,

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרוֹבֵעַ וְנִרְבָּע, בְּמוּקְצֶה וְנֶעֱבָד, בְּאֶתְנַן וּמְחִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more animals to the same list of animals that are fit for use but not fit for the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals involved in bestiality, animals connected to עבודה זרה, and an אתנן or מחיר are all unfit for the מזבח, so they cause a problem when mixed with קרבנות.
